title: Rainwater Harvesting: A Lifeline for Human Well-Being
claim: Small-scale, decentralised rainwater harvesting and retention infrastructure, such as earth ponds, stone dikes, and cisterns, can increase water availability and rehabilitate watersheds without eroding the ecosystem functions water serves in the local landscape.
evidence_text: UNEP and the Stockholm Environment Institute's report on rainwater harvesting examines the potential for greater use of small-scale, decentralised rainfall harvesting and storage within integrated water resource management. It documents that ecologically sensitive rainwater retention infrastructure — earth ponds, stone dikes, and cisterns — has helped rehabilitate watersheds and improve water use efficiency and availability, putting into practice ecosystem-based approaches to climate adaptation.
